title: Redwood discovery - model selection (Pacifica AI)
summary: Initial discovery focused on model selection for multi-lingual customer-facing assistant. Discussed context-length needs, open model tradeoffs, tool-calling, and deployment options (hosted vs dedicated vs private/VPC). Agreed to run a short benchmark on a sample prompt set; AE to send pricing + security pack; technical deep-dive scheduled.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-13
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Samantha Park (Redwood AE), Omar Haddad (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (CTO, Pacifica AI), Marcus Yu (ML Eng), Priya Singh (Infra)

Auto-generated summary: discuss model selection for multi-lingual assistant, context length, deployment options, security.

[00:00] Samantha: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh this is Samantha from Redwood. Happy to have Omar our SE on, he will cover the deeper perf and model questions. How's everyone doing?
[00:15] Lena: Good thanks, um we appreciate you carving time. We are evaluating Redwood because we need predictable latency for a multi-lingual assistant across hosted and private options.
[00:28] Marcus: Yeah, morning. Quick context: our app supports 12 languages, we have long-form user conversations so 32k-ish context would be ideal for some flows, others are shorter. We also need function/tool calling to hit internal APIs.
[00:42] Omar: Great, thanks Marcus. So quick clarifying q: when you say 32k, is that tokens or characters roughly, and is it continuous KV cache usage or more discrete session windows?
[00:55] Marcus: Tokens. Mostly continuous for a session - users chat across 30+ turns. We do prefix system messages + user history. So the KV needs to persist across calls or we need efficient offloading.
[01:10] Omar: Understood. On Redwood side we have models and routing that support longer contexts; depending on the model family we can hit 32k effectively with certain compiled kernels and kv cache strategies. For cost reasons sometimes teams split longer context into embedding-based retrievals to reduce token cost.
[01:30] Samantha: Wanted to surface two deployment options up front: Hosted (our managed API) gives fastest onboarding; Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools and predictable throughput; Private/VPC is available for stricter compliance. Which of those are you leaning to?
[01:46] Lena: For now, likely Dedicated or Private - we have regulated customers in EU and need data residency controls. But we'd like a hosted pilot first, if possible.
[01:58] Priya: Yeah network policies and SSO matter - we need SAML/Okta, KMS integration for customer-managed keys, and audit logs. Does Redwood support HSM or KMS integration?
[02:12] Omar: Yes - we integrate with KMS providers and have HSM-backed key options for Private deployments. Audit logs and retention policies can be configured, and we provide SOC 2 docs. I'll attach the security whitepaper after the call.
[02:28] Marcus: Great. On models, we're evaluating open models. Our shortlist: Mistral X/XL, Llama 3 variants (orca-ish), MPT, Falcon, and RedPajama. We care about instruction-following, multilingual quality, and tool-calling stability. Any recommendations?
[02:48] Omar: Right, so tradeoffs: Mistral family has strong instruction performance but earlier MistralX had limited long-context variants; Llama 3 has good tool-calling and ecosystem, but licensing and quantization options vary. Falcon is good for long context in some variants. We (Redwood) verify performance profiles per model in our catalog. For multi-lingual, Mistral and Llama 3 family typically outperform older MPT on non-English.
[03:12] Samantha: I'll share our model comparison doc - it's the Redwood catalog with verified latencies and throughput per hardware (link: https://app.redwood.com/model-catalog).
[03:24] Lena: Awesome. For tool-calling - we need deterministic function call outputs that map to our typed APIs. How well do the open models do function-calling? We've seen mixed results.
[03:36] Omar: Function calling depends on the model's decoding behavior. Llama 3 and some Mistral variants are much better at structured function output. We also layer a post-processor and provide schema-enforced wrappers in the SDK to reduce hallucinations. For mission-critical calls we recommend schema + a light verification step.
[03:58] Marcus: Ok. Latency is important: our SLO is 600ms p95 for short prompts (<1k tokens). For long context requests we can accept more, but we need predictable tail latency. How do you handle batching vs latency?
[04:12] Omar: Redwood runtime supports continuous batching with latency SLO controls - you can configure per-route latency targets and we will favor small batches for low-latency routes. On Dedicated you can reserve capacity to avoid noisy neighbor issues.
[04:28] Priya: Any quantization guidance? We want to reduce cost but not degrade multilingual quality.
[04:36] Omar: We recommend int8 for many models; for Llama 3 some teams prefer q4 for best quality/efficiency tradeoffs. We can run A/B evals - Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization profiles by workload.
[04:52] Lena: Good. On data residency: we need EU-region private deployment. Is the private control plane fully customer-managed or do you have a hybrid control plane?
[05:04] Omar: For Private we offer a customer-managed control plane option where control plane sits in your VPC; there is a management plane we can optionally host but for strict residency we can do fully customer-hosted. We'll need to map network requirements in detail.
[05:20] Samantha: Quick question on scale: what qps are you expecting at peak?
[05:24] Marcus: For the first phase maybe 20qps sustained, spiky to 150 for big events. Mostly small messages but occasional long context generation.
[05:36] Omar: That's a good fit for Dedicated with autoscaling policies. We can set burst capacity for event peaks.
[05:44] Lena: Pricing-wise we care about per-token cost for hosted vs committed pricing for Dedicated. Can you send a breakdown?
[05:52] Samantha: Yes, I'll send hosted per-token and Dedicated reserved GPU pricing + an example TCO for your 20qps baseline.
[06:02] Marcus: On the model side - we're worried about model drift and reproducibility. How do you handle model versioning and rollbacks?
[06:12] Omar: Each model version is pinned; we support canary and A/B rollouts. You can pin a route to a specific model+quantization profile. We also keep KV cache compatibility notes.
[06:24] Priya: Do you keep logs of request/response for audit? What about redaction?
[06:30] Omar: Yes, audit logs at token-level are available; for sensitive data we recommend client-side redaction and KMS-managed encryption. We can also support retention policies per account.
[06:44] Lena: Ok, let's talk multilingual quality - especially for Japanese and Portuguese - do you have benchmark scores?
[06:52] Samantha: We have internal evals and can run a pilot using your prompts. I'll attach a sample eval spreadsheet after.
[07:02] Marcus: We'll provide representative prompts. Also: tool-calling reliability - do you support synchronous tool invocation through the SDK or is it asynchronous webhooks?
[07:12] Omar: SDK supports synchronous function calls; we also support asynchronous webhooks for long-running tools. For synchronous we run the call in-process and return structured JSON (if model cooperates) and fallback to post-processing.
[07:28] Lena: Any caveat with streaming and tool-calls simultaneously? We do streaming responses to the client and sometimes emit tool call events mid-stream.
[07:38] Omar: You can stream tokens and emit intermediate tool-call directives; on the server side we offer hooks to intercept streaming events. There are some models that don't handle mid-stream directives gracefully - we can help choose the right model.
[07:54] Marcus: About open models and license compatibility - some of our legal team flagged Llama 3 commercial terms. Have you seen issues in past deals?
[08:04] Samantha: Licensing is definitely a legal check. We usually advise working with our legal team early; for models with commercial restrictions we have alternatives in the catalog.
[08:16] Priya: On infra, our network team will need a list of ports/ips and a sample VPC peering doc. Can you provide that?
[08:24] Omar: Absolutely - I'll send the private deployment network checklist.
[08:30] [10-minute marker, small cross-talk while people grab docs]
[08:52] Lena: One thing: we have a use-case that needs vector DB retrieval + long context stitching. Does Redwood provide integrated retrieval augmentation or do you recommend an external vector store?
[09:04] Omar: We integrate with common vector stores but also provide prefix caching and retrieval hooks. For cost we often recommend RAG with smart windowing: keep embeddings for long history and only materialize relevant context into the prompt.
[09:20] Marcus: How about embeddings model recommendation for multi-lingual - do you offer multi-lingual embedding models or do customers run language-specific embeddings?
[09:28] Omar: We have multi-lingual open embedding models in the catalog; for highest fidelity some customers run language-specific embeddings for languages with lower support. We can recommend based on your prompt set after seeing examples.
[09:44] Samantha: Ok, let's sketch the pilot plan: 1) customer shares 10-15 prompts + languages and a small dataset, 2) Redwood runs a benchmark across 3 candidate models (we suggest Llama 3 mix, Mistral variant, and Falcon long-context), 3) we provide latency/cost/quality report and a recommendation. Sound good?
[10:06] Lena: Yes that works. Timeline?
[10:10] Samantha: We can turn around a quick benchmark in ~5 business days once we have prompts and a baseline config. Omar will own the bench.
[10:20] Marcus: I am curious on observed hallucination rates with function-calling across models - do you have metrics?
[10:28] Omar: We do internal metrics; function-calling hallucination is model dependent. We'll include hallucination/structure compliance in the bench report. Also, schema enforcement reduces erroneous outputs.
[10:40] Priya: For private deployment - what are typical provisioning times?
[10:46] Omar: Private customer-managed setup takes variable time; for our standard private package usually 4-6 weeks, can be faster with well-prepared infra. Dedicated can be faster if you accept hosted control plane.
[11:00] Lena: Ok. Any other blockers we should know about?
[11:04] Marcus: Data residency and legal sign-off are the main ones. Also we may want an option to run on-prem later.
[11:12] Samantha: We support on-prem packages for regulated workloads; we'll include that in the security pack.
[11:22] [12:00 marker - brief pause]
[11:36] Lena: For k/v caching and long sessions, are there best practices to avoid token blowup?
[11:44] Omar: Yes: summarization of older turns, embedding-based retrieval for long tail, and selective caching of system+important user messages. We can provide a reference design.
[11:56] Marcus: Also curious about costs for long contexts - if we stitch 32k context often what's the per-token cost impact?
[12:04] Omar: Cost scales with consumed tokens; for long context we recommend RAG or dedicated capacity plus KV caching to avoid sending full history each call. We'll model example TCO in the pricing sheet.
[12:20] Lena: Last area: observability - we need per-route latency and token cost breakdowns. Does Redwood expose that?
[12:28] Samantha: Yes, Redwood Console provides per-route dashboards, token-level cost breakdown, tracing hooks and error analysis. We can give a demo of the Console in the SE deep dive.
[12:40] Marcus: Perfect. Anything on model fine-tuning or adapters? We may want a small supervised fine-tune for our domain.
[12:48] Omar: We support fine-tuning for eligible models; for many open models we also support parameter-efficient adapters and instruction-tuning workflows. We'll include eligibility in the bench doc.
[13:00] Lena: Great. Let's confirm next steps and owners.
[13:06] Samantha: Recap - I'll send pricing, security docs, and the model catalog link. Omar will share the benchmark template and run the bench once you share prompts. Customer will provide prompts and infra constraints.
[13:20] Marcus: Sounds good. We'll aim to get prompts within 48 hours.
[13:28] Priya: We'll get network requirements to you by end of week.
[13:34] Samantha: Excellent. Thanks everyone. Omar, anything to add?
[13:38] Omar: Just that we'll propose 3 candidate models for the bench: Llama 3 mix (q4), a Mistral variant, and Falcon long-context, comparing multilingual metrics and function-calling compliance.
[13:56] Lena: Thanks. We'll review the docs when you send them.
[14:02] Samantha: Thanks all, I'll follow up with the deck and action items.
[14:06] [Call ends]

Notes: transcript contains minor transcription errors in proper nouns (redwood sometimes 'red wood'), fillers and overlapping speech. Shared artifacts: https://app.redwood.com/model-catalog, security whitepaper (to be attached), benchmark template (to be shared)
